cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's accounting machine reconcile the October bank account for HANGS Construction: matching the books to the bank statement, line by line.
First, it reads the bank statement and the books. Each adds up on its own.
Next, it checks that October starts exactly where September's signed reconciliation ended. It does, to the cent.
Four deposits match. One is in transit: too late for this statement.
An outstanding check is one written but not yet cashed; four are. One check was entered $27 short, two digits swapped.
Bank fees and interest aren't in the books yet. Once they are, the bank and the books agree to the cent.
Last, it writes the workpapers, the math behind every figure, and an unsigned memo for the controller, the head of accounting.

All done. The bank and the books agree at just over $1,029,000. Five items are open: three small journal entries, or corrections to the books, worth $70.47 in all, plus the $25,000 deposit in transit and a check over 90 days old that was never cashed. Nothing is posted; the controller reviews and signs.
